category_title: Verbal students with Asperger syndrome who engage in monologues and have visual impairments
scenario_title: Conversational interaction with peers without disabilities
minimal_context: Kaylie is participating in a 5-minute conversational interaction session with a peer without disabilities using a Braille communication book.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Kaylie, it is time for your 5-minute conversation session with your peer partner. Please use your Braille communication book to start.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Rubs her eyes) When I meet new people I’m sort of nervous.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Just try your best to pick a topic from the book.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Speaks in a continuous monologue without pausing) I listened to a new audio book yesterday about horses and there are so many different breeds of horses, some are very tall and some are small, and I think the small ones are interesting but the tall ones run faster and I want to learn more about them...

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Kaylie, you need to make a decision on which question to ask your partner now.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Begins rubbing her face and smelling the edge of the communication book) Well, I don’t know what I want! I never have enough time!

task.content: 5-minute conversational interaction sessions using communication books with peers
task.learning_goal: learning to talk to new friends at school

context.materials: communication books with conversational openers printed in Braille with the English equivalent printed underneath

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: when faced with making a decision or experiencing stress
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: engaged in stereotypic behavior, including smelling objects, self-talk, and rubbing her face
related_quotes: Well, I don’t know what I want! I never have enough time!

behavior_patterns.condition: When Kaylie interacted with peers without disabilities
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: typically spoke in a monologue, giving peers little opportunity to reciprocate
related_quotes: When I meet new people I’m sort of nervous.

behavior_patterns.condition: During baseline observations in general education classes and lunch
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: engage in repetitive stereotypic behavior, including hand and finger movements, eye rubbing, verbal stereotypy, repetitive handling of objects, and skin picking
